name: grid_co2e_g_per_mj_low
source: NOT a guidebook value: same source and table, row THG-Emissionen aus den Vorketten, year 2025 = 54 g CO2e/kWh / 3.6. This is a BOUND, NOT A SCENARIO: direct combustion set to zero, upstream left at the level of today. UBA publishes no citable 2045 electricity factor (checked 2026-09-03; its own 2026 projection leaves 212.5 Mt CO2e residual in 2045). A true renewables-mix upstream would have to be built from UBA CC 11/2026. METHODS-LOG 2.55

name: charging_loss_share
source: SETTING (user 2026-09-03): AC depot charging at 11 kW or more. ADAC measures 5.1-7.0 % at an 11 kW wallbox over five models (Renault R5 E-Tech 5.1 / Tesla Model Y 6.1 / Mercedes CLA 350 EQ 6.9 / VW ID.7 6.9 / Volvo EX30 7.0); the socket case 12.7-24.2 % is consumer charging and not our depot case. The EMEP BEV EC curve is VEHICLE-side consumption, so this loss sits between grid and battery and is applied ONLY in the CO2e chain -- ENERGY_MJ stays vehicle-side so that the ev_range_km_* derivation stays consistent with it. METHODS-LOG 2.55

name: aux_load_share_bev
source: SETTING (user 2026-09-08): constant BEV auxiliary load (cabin heating PLUS base auxiliaries: lights, blower, control units) as a share of traction energy, at ambient_temp_c = 10 degC. 0.15 of 9.2 kW traction power = 1.38 kW continuous. Band at 10 degC: heat pump 0.3-0.75 kW, resistive 0.8-1.5 kW, base auxiliaries 0.3-0.5 kW -- 1.38 kW is the SUM and sits in the upper half, which the door opening frequency of DRT service justifies (9148 rides plus 892 freight stops per day). NOT a heating-only figure. Applied ONLY to bev: a diesel takes cabin heat from waste heat. Applied per km although the physical effect is per hour -- all arms sit in a 36-38 km/h band, so this does not shift the arm comparison. Diesel has no counterpart because EMEP carries none. METHODS-LOG 2.57

name: kg_per_parcel
source: ASSUMPTION, deliberately rounded (user 2026-07-31). Order of magnitude supported by three sources: Amaral et al. 2026, 'Empirical analysis of e-commerce delivery operations: from parcels to tours', Transportation Research Part E, Tab. 1 -> mean 1.6478 kg (only measured mean; BRAZILIAN data, declared transfer); Rajendran & Harper 2021, 'Simulation-based algorithm for determining best package delivery alternatives under three criteria: Time, cost and sustainability', TRIP -> 1-350 lbs, >50 % under 5 lbs (no mean given); Mohri, Nassir, Lavieri & Thompson 2024, 'Modeling package delivery acceptance in Crowdshipping systems by Public Transportation Passengers: A latent class approach', Travel Behaviour and Society 35, 100716 -> 0.5-5 kg. MEAN not median - total on-board mass = n x mean; Amaral median 0.6950 would understate by 58 %. Plausible band on the mean 1.3-2.5 kg (~16 pp on the allocation share at 50 parcels)
